name: LEGO® style
touchpoints: how LEGO® shows a number to a shopper, and the bricks themselves: the bricks (stacked 2px apart, flat studs on top, clear bricks beside the colours), the LEGO Group's performance highlights (results drawn as columns of stacked bricks, the value over each column), the lego.com shop at Black Friday (the yellow header band; yellow badges with 4px corners such as New, Exclusives and Retiring soon; red % OFF badges; the sale price in red beside the struck-out price; the box line 18+ | set | pieces; the orange Add to Bag pill), and the gifts with purchase that LEGO® gives at set basket values over the Insiders Weekend and Black Friday

devices.stack: Figure 1, brick towers: what each event added over the year before, and this year's plan built brick by brick. A grey 4px baseplate is 0 (the same as the year before). Past events (2023–2025) are towers of flat grey #a3a3a3 bricks, a full brick a fixed number of sets (100K for all channels and online, 50K for stores; a top brick under 35% of a full one joins the brick below), 2px apart, two flat studs on top. Then one brick a driver, each starting where the last one ended: shoppers #1e5aa8 (more members, wishlists), offers #e05a00 (gifts, 2× points), new sets #f7c600 with a #b38f00 edge; a driver that takes sets off (fewer discounts) is a white brick with a 2px #e05a00 dashed edge and dashed studs, its value under it. Thin #8a8a8a dashed connectors run between the drivers at the running total. Last, the plan: a wider tower (1.8 columns, four studs) of white bricks with a 2px #2c2c2c edge, its value in 30px/800 under a #ffd502 badge with the event total (2.90M in total). A value over every column: past events 13px (the last year 700, the rest muted), drivers 14.5px/800, signed (+150K, −200K). Under the axis the year, the driver name on up to two lines (a shorter name if it would be cut) and the plan in bold
devices.tag: sale tags, from the lego.com shop: Figure 2 puts each offer's lego.com badge as its label (Gift with purchase on #ffd502, 2× points white with a #2c2c2c edge, 20% OFF and 30% OFF on #dd0000 with white 700 text, Free shipping on #f2f2f2), where it applies under it in 12.5px muted, and the extra sets per $1,000 of offer cost as a long flat brick with one stud per 5 sets (planned offers #e05a00, dropped offers #a3a3a3), the value at the end in 26px/800. The KPI row writes offer cost as a price tag: this year's share big, last year's struck out beside it in 22px/700 #141414; a shortfall is a red badge (3 short). Table 1 prices the hero sets the lego.com way: a red #bd0000 sale price beside the struck-out price, with the offer's badge above
devices.ladder: Figure 3, the gift ladder: last year's orders as $10 basket bars, coloured by the gift step they reach (no gift #a3a3a3, then #f3a07d, #ea7f4e, #e05a00 for $40, $100 and $200); the last bar ($300 and over) half a bar apart. A #fff1b0 band under the $20 before each step shows the orders a small add-on would lift. Each step is a 1.5px #2c2c2c line with a #ffd502 badge flag (Gift 1 · $40; $40 alone when the next step is close) and the share of orders that reach it in 20px/800
devices.shop: the lego.com shop parts around the figures: the 56px #ffd502 header band with the company and report and the EN/KO pill in white; a strip with the yellow Plan · Nov 9 badge and the event dates; the channel filter in #f2f2f2 pills with the selected one #2c2c2c; KPI boxes and cards in white with 1px #d9d9d9 lines and 8px corners; the box line in Table 1 (18+ in a 1.5px outlined box with 4px corners | set | pieces); the one orange #f47d20 pill (Get one made) with #141414 text

sample.topic: Black Friday 2026 plan of Vizney Toys, a fictional brick-toy maker, in the US, as of Nov 9: the event is the members' weekend (Nov 21–22) and Black Friday to Cyber Monday (Nov 27–30), online and in its brand stores. Sets sold at the 2022–2025 events and the drivers that take 2025 to the 2026 target of 2.90M sets (more members, wishlists, gifts with purchase, 2× points, new sets, fewer discounts), offer tests as extra sets per $1,000 of offer cost, last year's orders by basket value against the $40, $100 and $200 gift steps, orders by hour over the six days with this year's plan, and 12 hero sets by stock and inbound against event demand. Every set name and number is invented and the figures are not real

canvas.role: page, boxes and the plot: lego.com's white

header.role: the header band (56px; lego.com's is 60px), the date badge, the plan badge in Figure 1, the gift-step flags in Figure 3, the plan's numbered badges in Figure 4. Only ink sits on it: #141414 13.0:1

line.role: 1px box outlines, KPI dividers: lego.com's product tile line. No shadows on boxes

ink.role: titles, values, the selected pill (white text 14.0:1), step lines in Figure 3, the plan's edge in Figure 1, plan outlines in Figure 4

muted.role: subtitles, notes, axis ticks, set numbers (6.0:1): lego.com's element ID grey

pill.role: filter and secondary pills, 40px, 999px corners: lego.com's Filter and Sort pills

button.role: the one primary pill (Get one made), text #141414 6.8:1: lego.com's Add to Bag on the Black Friday page

button-text.role: text on the orange pill and on badges

side.role: the package list in the build bench; hovered rows

baseplate.role: the 4px baseplate under Figure 1, the zero line

sale.role: % OFF badges and shortfall badges with white 700 text (5.2:1): lego.com's sale badge

sale-text.role: sale prices and shortfalls in text (6.6:1 on white): lego.com's sale price

near.role: the band under the $20 before each gift step in Figure 3; never under text

status.role: a good change is Bright Blue with ▲ or ▼ by direction; red only for a shortfall (stock under demand) and for sale badges; the KPI arrows show direction, the colour shows good or bad

tiers.role: Figure 3: no gift, gift 1 ($40), gift 2 ($100), gift 3 ($200). The three oranges are one hue light to dark

heat.role: Figure 4: the share of event orders in each hour, under 0.1% (stores closed, the small hours) in #f2f2f2, then the five blues. The legend is the six cells with 0.1 · 0.4 · 0.8 · 1.2 · 1.8% under the borders

text.role: values and labels stay in ink; changes in blue when good and red when bad, always with ▲ ▼ and a word

validation.tool: dataviz validate_palette.js (OKLab), mode light, surface #ffffff, run 2026-11-18
validation.categorical: Bright Blue #1e5aa8, orange #e05a00, Bright Yellow #f7c600 and grey #a3a3a3, all pairs: worst CVD ΔE 15.1 (deutan, grey and orange), normal-vision ΔE 20.2. The yellow is outside the lightness band on purpose (L 0.85) and the grey reads grey on purpose: yellow bricks carry a #b38f00 edge and a value, grey is past events only
validation.sequential: #89b5f2 · #6f9edf · #5587cd · #3a70ba · #1e5aa8 --ordinal: one hue, monotone, every step ΔL ≥ 0.06, light end 2.05:1 on white
validation.diverging: arms checked apart --ordinal: orange #f3a07d · #ea7f4e · #e05a00 and blue #89b5f2 · #5587cd · #1e5aa8 pass; mirrored steps differ under CVD (ΔE 16.4, 19.9, 24.4); midpoint #e8e8e8
validation.status: #1e5aa8 · #bd0000 · #a3a3a3 all pairs: worst CVD ΔE 22.3, normal 27.9
validation.text: on white: ink 14.0, body 10.9, muted 6.0, blue #1e5aa8 6.8, orange text #b04f00 5.3, sale red #bd0000 6.6; white on the #dd0000 badge 5.2; #141414 on #ffd502 13.0 and on #f47d20 6.8
validation.marks: orange #e05a00 bars 3.7:1 on white; the light marks (#f7c600 1.6:1, #a3a3a3 2.5:1, the light heat and tier steps 2.0:1) carry a value, an edge or a table view

code.note: the screen's text steps and two brick colours; every token is 5.5:1 or more on #f7f7f7 and on the highlight

sans.role: every word and number, one body face per language. Gantari stands in for Cera Pro, which lego.com uses (at 100px the cap height is 67 against 66 and the same string is 796.1 against 795.6px wide). lego.com/ko-kr sets Korean in Noto Sans KR, so Korean screens use Noto Sans KR alone. Cera Pro is not used

scale.headline: 30px/800 (ko 28px/700), line-height 1.22; 24px under 640px
scale.card-title: 19px/700 (ko 18px), the figure number above it 12.5px/700 muted
scale.kpi: 52px/800 tabular (ko 700); 46px under 1360px (42px at 1200–1279px), 34px under 640px; label 14px/600 above, unit 22px/700 beside, change 13.5px under
scale.figure-1: values 14.5px/800 on drivers, 13px on past events, the plan 30px/800 under a 24px badge; names 12.5px, two lines at most
scale.figure-2: badges 12.5px in 24px; where it applies 12.5px muted; values 26px/800, 'sets' 13px muted on the first row
scale.figure-3: flags 12px/700 in 22px badges; the share that reaches each step 20px/800 with 'reach it' 12.5px muted; axis 12px
scale.figure-4: days 12.5px (Black Friday 700), hours 12px every three hours, numbered badges 11px/800 in a 17px circle
scale.table: name 15px/700, box line 12.5px (age 11.5px/700 in a 1.5px outlined box with 4px corners | set | pieces), numbers 16px/700, prices 15px/700

typography.notation: sets in K and M (70K, 2.90M) and in 만 in Korean (7만, 290만; under 10K in 천: 9천); drivers and added sets signed (+150K, −200K); dollars as $149M and $249.99 (Korean 1.49억 달러, 9,912만 달러, 249.99달러); percent whole in titles and changes (17%), one decimal for shares and cost (6.4%); points as pts (ko %p); ▲ ▼ before every change

rows: header 56px, yellow: Vizney Toys and the report name, the EN/KO pill in white
strip: the yellow Plan · Nov 9 badge | Members' weekend Nov 21–22 | Black Friday to Cyber Monday Nov 27–30, with the channel filter on the right (All channels | Online | Brand stores)
KPI row: Black Friday target, revenue target, offer cost with last year struck out, hero sets ready with a red shortfall badge
first screen (1440×810): Figure 1, brick towers | Figure 2, sale tags (560px). Bottoms on one line
Running the event: Figure 3, the gift ladder | Figure 4, orders by hour with the plan; then Table 1, hero sets, least covered first, eight rows and the rest on demand
Build it yourself · How we count (seven definitions) · footer
layout.responsive: 1200–1359: right column 520px; Figure 1 keeps the last two events and short names under 600px. Under 1200: Figures 1 and 2, then 3 and 4, stacked across the page; Figure 2 as tall as its rows. Under 1024: KPI 2×2. Under 900: Table 1 drops stock. Under 640: one column, the channel filter in three equal pills, Figure 1 names at an angle under 400px, Table 1 keeps set, offer and covered

motion.bricks: 0.34s drop from 14px above with a small settle. Figure 1: past towers brick by brick, 70ms a column and 55ms a brick, the drivers after, the plan last, then the values and badge fade in. Figure 3: bars drop 18ms apart
motion.grow: 0.5s, Figure 2's bricks grow from the left, 90ms apart, the values fade in after
motion.fade: 0.3s; Figure 4's tiles fade in by hour and day

tableau.fonts: Tableau Book for text; Gantari only if installed on every viewing machine and the server

measured.date: 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15 (home, product pages, Pick a Brick, performance highlights, Fair Play) and 2026-11-18 (the US Sale page and the Black Friday 2026 page), built-in browser
measured.shop: header band #ffd502 60px with #2c2c2c text; product tiles white with 1px #d9d9d9 lines and 8px corners; box line 18+ | pieces | rating; element ID text 12px #636363; Cera Pro (Noto Sans KR on ko-kr)
measured.sale: badges 24px high, 4px corners, 12px text, a 1px white edge: yellow #ffd502 with #141414 500 text (New, Exclusives, Retiring soon), red #dd0000 with white 700 text (20% OFF); sale price #bd0000 16px/700 beside the struck-out price #141414; Add to Bag #f47d20 with #141414 text, 40px pill; the Sale page sits on #750002 with a #9b0000 hero tile, 12px corners
measured.black-friday: Black Friday 2026 runs Nov 27 to Cyber Monday Nov 30; the Insiders Weekend is Nov 21–22; offers are discounts, gifts with purchase at set basket values and extra points. The Black Friday page is black with red brick lettering (not used)
measured.report: the performance highlights draw revenue and profit as columns of bricks with the value over each column
measured.not_used: the logo, minifigures, the LEGO wordmark or any lettering on studs, the Black Friday page's black and red brick art, photos and renders of sets or stores, real sets, set numbers and theme names, the real gifts, slogans, Cera Pro

notice.why: LEGO's Fair Play page asks for this sentence, for LEGO® as an adjective with ® every time, for no logo on unofficial sites and for no LEGO in web addresses. The style, its folder and its slugs carry the LEGO name by the owner's decision (2026-11-14); if the LEGO Group objects, the name, folder and posts change together
